mcp.tool.scan:
Scans all scan roots and returns each file's state, elapsed days, flags, and allowed_actions.

Specifying ``project`` narrows the result to that project name (symmetric with sweep/promote).
mcp.tool.find: Free-form search. Uses the same AND contract as the CLI ``docsweep find`` and can also filter by target_release.
mcp.tool.set_target_release: Atomically updates only the target_release of an existing MD (does not change the settings).
mcp.tool.list_projects: Lists the projects and whether each one is enabled or excluded (UX W2 / P39).
mcp.tool.set_project_enabled: Excludes a project from the board/scan (enabled=False) or restores it.
mcp.tool.route_intent:
Maps a natural-language intent to a docsweep subcommand (UX W2 / P28).

Typical: "what did I do yesterday", "continue today's work", "open the board", "undo"
mcp.tool.doctor: Environment health check (config / roots / index / inject). Same as the CLI ``docsweep doctor``.
mcp.tool.day: Opens or closes the day. phase is open (morning) or close (night).
mcp.tool.brief:
Morning entry point: settles on the one thing to do today. Same contract as the CLI ``docsweep brief``.

Typical user utterances: "continue today's work", "give me a brief", "morning status", "what should I do?",
"status of all projects" (``all_projects=True``).

By default it returns a single entry for the cwd project (inferred from the git remote). ``all_projects=True``
lays out all of ``search_paths`` side by side (an overview equivalent to cross).

Returns:
    ``{{mode, generated_at, projects: [{{project, today_pick, co_running, watchouts,
    yesterday_done, open_count, stale_count}}]}}``. ``today_pick`` is the single
    highest-scoring item, and the AI may treat it as "the work to start next".
mcp.tool.capture_extract:
Extracts plan / bugfix / pending draft candidates from the conversation history ``text``.

Typical user utterances: "make this a plan", "capture the previous conversation into docsweep",
"make this bug a bugfix", "put this on hold".

``use_llm=False`` uses the heuristic path (decision-marker detection). ``use_llm=True`` uses an LLM
provider (currently only ``mock`` is implemented).

Returns: ``{{drafts: [{{id, kind, title, body, suggested_filename, source_hint,
project, tags}}], count}}``. If there are candidates to adopt, call ``capture_save`` next.
mcp.tool.capture_save:
Adopts drafts obtained from ``capture_extract`` and saves them under the configured work_dir.

Typical user utterances: "adopt them", "adopt 2 and 3", "save them all as plans".

``drafts`` accepts the ``drafts`` returned by ``capture_extract`` as-is (the AI is expected to
narrow it down to the subset the user wants to adopt). Returns: ``{{saved: [path...], count}}``.
mcp.tool.cross:
Bundles all projects, settles on a single "today's pick", and lists the freezer queue.

Typical user utterances: "status of all projects", "show me the cross view", "which project should I
start with?", "show the freezer queue", "any archive candidates?".

``projects=['a','b']`` narrows the target projects (all of search_paths when omitted).

Returns:
    ``{{generated_at, project_filter, top_pick, runners_up[], frozen_candidates[],
    project_summaries[{{project, open_count, stale_count, today_one}}],
    total_projects, total_open}}``. ``top_pick`` is a single item, and the AI may treat it as
    "the work to start next overall". ``frozen_candidates`` are recommended for archiving.
mcp.tool.triage:
Remaining-work view for the start of a session. Narrows to needs-decision and pending items, oldest first, and returns each
item with rel/title/state/type/age_days and machine-executable actions ("the work to do next" comes first
even if you don't remember the file names). Broken labels are attached separately in needs_fix.

Specifying ``project`` returns the subset for that project (counts are per-project as well).
mcp.tool.sweep:
Moves done/discarded files to each project's archive/ (does not touch watching).

Specifying ``project`` narrows it to that project name (symmetric with promote).
mcp.tool.promote:
Promotes watching items to done and moves them to the archive.

With due_expired_only=True, only watching items whose due date has arrived (including today) are targeted.
mcp.tool.index: Regenerates the cross-project INDEX, writes it to .docsweep/, and returns the counts.
mcp.tool.summary:
Compressed JSON to hand to the AI (an INDEX narrowed to the key points of needs-decision, pending, and needs-fix items).

Specifying ``project`` returns the subset for that project.
mcp.tool.inject:
Injects docsweep's operating rules (managed blocks + .docsweep.yaml) into the specified project.

If the guidance lives in the global settings, include_guidance=False limits it to the label section
(equivalent to the CLI --no-guidance). write_yaml=False does not write .docsweep.yaml (equivalent to --no-yaml).
lang ({langs}) sets the language of the injected text. If omitted, the language of that project's documents is used
(the lang setting, or the display language if unset).
mcp.tool.eject: Removes the injected managed blocks (hand-written text is kept).
mcp.tool.inject_global:
Injects the guidance to read triage at session start and the due rules into the AI tool's global settings (effective in all projects).

If lang ({langs}) is omitted, it writes in the lang setting, or the display language if unset.
mcp.tool.eject_global: Removes the guidance block injected into the global settings.
mcp.tool.update_status:
Rewrites the MD's H1 label to ``new_status``.

``new_status`` accepts a status label ("Planned" / "In Progress" / "Watching" /
"Pending" / "Done" / "Discarded", or the same labels in Japanese) or an internal state key.
The former bugfix-only label (Japanese for "in progress") is still accepted as an alias of "In Progress"
(active was merged into in-progress in the 2026-06-23 revision).
When ``[Done]`` / ``[Discarded]`` is specified, it internally calls ``archive_done`` and moves the file to the archive
in one go (on the premise that the MCP call carries the same decision as a human click).
``watching_days`` is a one-time override of the due days, used only when moving to watching.
mcp.tool.update_due:
Rewrites the frontmatter ``due:`` and increments ``postpone_count`` by 1.

``new_due`` is ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or ``today`` / ``+1d`` / ``+1w`` / ``+1m``.
A past date only produces a warning and is not rejected (the item just stays in the Overdue column).
mcp.tool.update_content:
Replaces the entire MD body (supports optimistic locking).

A mismatched ``expected_mtime`` is returned as ``kind=conflict``. Required when called from the Web UI.
mcp.tool.archive_done:
Moves ``[Done]`` / ``[Discarded]`` files to the archive.

Specifying ``paths`` moves them individually; ``auto=True`` moves all projects at once. If neither is given,
it errs on the safe side and does nothing (empty result). ``[Watching]`` is rejected even when specified explicitly (to protect resting items).
